assessments.reasoning: The exact CHM transcript p.36 describes variants of flip-flops and the simulation cost of using longer RTL descriptions. On p.51 Moorby recounts a generalized combinational UDP and a simple sequential UDP with a single state for flip-flop modeling.

challenge.method: Compare the two cited historical discussions and p.51's event-driven timing caveat. Test whether single state means a single possible state, whether the motivation was a synthesis guarantee, and whether the discussion claims universal flip-flop coverage.
challenge.results: The account concerns one stored state in a sequential primitive, alongside a combinational form. He describes simulation speed as a motivation and notes sensitivity to evaluation order. Neither a measured speedup nor universal device coverage follows.

limitations: This is Moorby's design recollection about simulation models. Standard UDP syntax, values, scheduling and synthesizability require exact separate evidence.
